miscarriage_by_maternal_age.source: Magnus MC, Wilcox AJ, Morken NH, Weinberg CR, Haberg SE. Role of maternal age and pregnancy history in risk of miscarriage: prospective register based study. BMJ 2019;364:l869. doi:10.1136/bmj.l869
miscarriage_by_maternal_age.quoted: The risk of miscarriage was lowest in women aged 25-29 (10%), and rose rapidly after age 30, reaching 53% in women aged 45 and over.

scenario_curves.flat_12: 0.12 at every age; isolates the selection mechanism from the age gradient of loss
scenario_curves.flat_30: 0.30 at every age; allows for unrecognized early losses that register data do not count
scenario_curves.age_graded: approximate reading of the published age curve: 15-19 0.16, 20-24 0.11, 25-29 0.10, 30-34 0.12, 35-39 0.17, 40-44 0.33, 45 0.53; intermediate values are scenario inputs, to be checked against the source tables before release
scenario_curves.steep: 0.10 through age 29 rising linearly to 0.53 at 45

smoking_and_miscarriage.source: Pineles BL, Park E, Samet JM. Systematic review and meta-analysis of miscarriage and maternal exposure to tobacco smoke during pregnancy. Am J Epidemiol 2014;179(7):807-823.
smoking_and_miscarriage.dose: about 1% increase in relative risk per cigarette per day

birth_certificate_smoking_ascertainment.source: PRAMS Working Group. Completeness of ascertainment of prenatal smoking using birth certificates and confidential questionnaires. Am J Epidemiol 1998;148(11):1046-1054.
birth_certificate_smoking_ascertainment.quoted_range: 70.6% to 82.0% of smoking captured on birth certificates versus 86.2% to 90.3% on confidential questionnaires

latent_type_scenarios.note: Illustrative values; the type is not observed and no prior is claimed.
